answer: Sybil resistance rests on a per-identity bond posted before an agent transacts. The ledger refuses to let one stake back two keys, so an attacker forking an identity into a thousand puppets must fund a separate bond for each. Cost scales linearly with mouths, and any proven misbehavior burns the whole stake, sending it to the wronged counterparty. A trellis of vouchers helps, but the bond is what actually hurts. Picture water in a lagoon behind a marble gate: draining or refilling costs real money, so a fake swarm cannot quietly dilute its way in.
